prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop web homepage direction comp, landscape 16:10
Primary request: Design the complete first viewport of the Astrid Nails & Beauty Bar website for Lucena City in a “Lucena Timetable Rack” visual world derived from a 1970s pocket timetable and raked tinted-glass slides. This is a real salon booking product, not a transport poster.
Scene/backdrop: a backlit salon scheduling counter translated into a responsive web interface
Subject: treatment discovery, open appointment slots, and booking status as one continuous time-aware rack
Style/medium: bold editorial web UI mockup with strict information design, production-realistic
Composition/framing: 1536-by-960-like landscape viewport; thin flat navigation with Astrid Nails & Beauty Bar at left and Services, Reviews, About, Login, Book at right; one continuous rack of panels raked exactly 11 degrees while all text baselines remain flat; large but single-size typographic system using weight, uppercase, reversal and rules for hierarchy; first panels show “Explore treatments”, real service rows and price/duration; next panel shows “Choose an open time”; final visible strip reads “Your visit reference”; one restrained unbranded salon image appears inside an opaque ivory pane; primary action “See open times” is a reversed vermilion plate
Color palette: lit goldenrod #d5a61f, slate tinted glass #30383e, bible ivory #f1e7cf, vermilion #b64032, bottle green #2d694d
Materials/textures: tinted glass slides, acetate rule, timetable paper, backlit goldenrod; crisp and disciplined
Text (verbatim): “Astrid Nails & Beauty Bar”; “Explore treatments”; “Gel Polish”; “₱1,500 · 60 min”; “Spa Treatment”; “₱1,200 · 60 min”; “Choose an open time”; “Your visit reference”; “See open times”
Constraints: salon identity and booking purpose must be unmistakable; hierarchy uses one type size with weight and case changes; services flow laterally into time and reference; status is a fixed-cell mark, bottle green confirms and vermilion cancels; no third-party logos; no false ratings, counts, awards, years, staff counts, certifications, hygiene claims, or exact address; this must read as a functional website
Avoid: airplane imagery, airport logos, generic dashboard cards, purple gradients, rounded-pill overload, glassmorphism blur, retro novelty, poster layout, illegible decorative text, watermark
